data.mechanism: A second and contested way in: JEW2015 reports that glutamine activates mTORC1 without the Rag GTPases, through Arf1, and that leucine and glutamine therefore do not share one entry point. If it holds, Rag-dependent lysosomal recruitment is not the only route to the kinase.
data.mechanism_beginner: Some experiments say glutamine has a second way in that skips the Rag proteins entirely. If that is right, the lysosome story is not the whole story – which is a big claim resting on thin evidence.
data.boundary: Cell-type dependent and not uniformly reproduced across labs. The Rag-dependent route is the separate GLN-RAG edge; neither edge should be read as covering the other.

conflict.basis: The mirror of GLN-RAG, and a head-to-head disagreement rather than two different contexts. JEW2015 reports that glutamine activates mTORC1 in cells lacking RagA and RagB (MEFs and HEK293A), through Arf1 and the v-ATPase but not Ragulator. DUR2012 reports the opposite dependence in comparable mammalian cells: inhibiting glutaminolysis prevented RagB GTP loading and mTORC1 translocation, placing the glutamine signal upstream of the Rags (GLN-RAG). Each edge lists the other's study as conflicting. The Atlas does not settle whether the two routes act in parallel or in different settings.
